# Whimbrel Research data

Machine-readable data on US medtech company activity: NIH SBIR/STTR
awards, FDA 510(k) clearances, and FDA PMA approvals, read daily from
the public registries. Every event links to the public record it came
from; an event that cannot be verified against a public source is not
published. Events carry the people the registry itself names in the
record, with no contact details; see /methodology.md.

The archive behind these files tracks 7284 US medtech companies and
runs back years. The files here are a rolling 14-day window.
The complete archive is available two ways: queryable free, a company
or a search at a time, over MCP and HTTP below, or as one file at
https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev/signals-archive.json, priced by the x402 catalogue at
https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev/.well-known/x402.

## Files

- /index.json: manifest of every file here, with schema version,
  license, and next-update time.
- /signals-latest.json: events observed in the last 14 days.
  Each event carries a stable id, company name, kind, event date,
  observed date, amount_usd where a source states a figure, a one-line
  summary, the source URL, and any people the registry names.
  Updated daily.
- /stats.json: aggregate history (weekly counts and stated dollars for
  the trailing quarter) and archive scale. Aggregates only.
- https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev/signals-archive.json: the complete archive as one
  file, same event schema as signals-latest.json. Served by the worker
  and priced by the x402 catalogue; not mirrored on the free static
  host. Updated daily.
- /methodology.md: how the data is collected, dated, and windowed, what
  it holds about people, and what these files exclude.

## MCP server

The same data is queryable over the Model Context Protocol
(Streamable HTTP; the free tools need no key) at:

https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev

Free tools, no key:

latest_signals, signal_of_the_day, weekly_pulse, who_got_funded,
find_signals, micro_brief, company_timeline, about_the_data,
get_access

latest_signals is the 14-day window, filterable by kind.
find_signals searches the whole archive by kind, date, text, amount,
and NIH phase. who_got_funded filters the window for fresh money.
micro_brief is a composed mini-dossier on any company in the archive
and company_timeline is the structured version of the same; those two
are capped at 100 company lookups per caller
per day. weekly_pulse and signal_of_the_day are computed views, and
about_the_data returns this document.

The server also publishes seven ready-made prompts, named with a
whimbrel_ prefix (whimbrel_micro_brief, whimbrel_latest_signals, ...), so
clients that surface prompts as slash commands get a command palette on
connect.

## HTTP API

The same handlers answer GET at the same origin, for readers that do
not speak MCP:

- /v1/signals/latest: the last 14 days of signals, filterable by kind
- /v1/signals/search: search the whole archive
- /v1/signals/funded: the window filtered for fresh money
- /v1/signals/today: the newest single signal
- /v1/pulse: seven-day aggregates
- /v1/company/{company}: every registry event for one company
- /v1/company/{company}/brief: a composed mini-dossier, as markdown

/v1/subscribe redirects to Stripe checkout for the paid tier, and
/v1/key/<checkout-session-id> hands over the resulting API key once.

Discovery and terms are free and always will be: https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev/.well-known/x402
carries the machine-readable catalogue of routes, prices, and whether
payment is currently on, and https://whimbrel-signals-mcp.whimbrelresearch.workers.dev/v1/about carries the terms in prose.
The catalogue is the authority on price; do not cache a number from
this file.

## The paid layer

A Whimbrel key unlocks the same server's remaining tools:

deep_record, research_status, matches_for_us, build_profile,
set_preferences, billing_portal

deep_record points the research pipeline at any company you name and
runs it on Whimbrel's infrastructure: current leadership, contact
routes, funding and milestones read from the company's own site and
press, every line quoted from the source it came from. research_status
tracks a queued run. build_profile reads your own firm's website and
drafts your capability profile, set_preferences stores your screening
decisions, and matches_for_us then returns the companies in the archive
that fit what your firm actually does.

To get a key, call get_access, which is free and needs no key, open the
Stripe checkout link it returns, and the page you land on shows an API
key once. Send that key as an Authorization Bearer header.
billing_portal returns the Stripe portal for card changes, upgrades and
cancellation.

## Done-for-you research

Everything above is self-serve. For a handful of medical device
engineering firms, Whimbrel does all the research: tell us what you
want and we research it, and a continuous watch on these same
registries flags new companies that fit what the firm builds. A person
reviews everything before it goes out. A sample of the research is at
https://whimbrelresearch.com/sample-brief/
The first month is free. https://whimbrelresearch.com
